rationale: bugs_open/394, the SECOND half of what the owner commissioned on 2026-08-25 (decision 4): the reader for RENDER_AUDIT_TRUNCATED existed but nothing ran it. The cursor half is fixed, live and accepted - [MEASURED 2026-09-02] the union of audited_paths over three consecutive SCHEDULED runs on webdesign.co.uk is 151 distinct pages of 151 live, ZERO missed, and the third run cleared the cursor. But `kubectl get cronjob` showed no render-truncation-check, so finding_code_registry.json's `consumed` claim was true about the code and false about the estate - exactly the state DBG-075 exists to prevent, and the only reason the bug is not closeable. This adds the CronJob (07:50 UTC, slot proven free against the REPO census, not kubectl), its dockerfile shipping the acks file in-image from committed HEAD, the overlay pinned like every sibling, the makefile RELEASE_IMAGES/AGENT_DEPLOY_SERVICES entries, and the hand-run wrapper the reader's own error messages already name. THE SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE IS DORMANCY, and it was found by the prescribed wire test rather than by design: running the reader against live data BEFORE shipping it returned exit 1 on loancalculator.co.uk, reporting that the migration-660 config flip had regressed. It had not. That site has ONE truncation row, from 2026-08-11, written under a per-dispatch max_pages:5 override, and it has 28 live pages against a cap of 60 - so it CANNOT truncate again and that row is frozen history. Arm (a) judged 'the most recent row in the group' and would have been red on day one and every day after, which is the one thing this estate says reliably turns a check off. A group whose newest row is more than 14 days behind the FLEET's newest is now reported as dormant and not judged. 14 days is ~4 missed opportunities at the 3-day per-site rotation cadence, so a genuine regression still produces recent rows and still alarms. Measured relative to the newest row in the dataset rather than the wall clock, so the rule is a pure function of the data and a fixture exercises it without a clock.

plan.summary: Ship the commissioned RENDER_AUDIT_TRUNCATED reader as a daily CronJob, and correct the one defect the pre-ship wire test found: a site that has STOPPED truncating freezes its last row for ever, so judging 'the most recent row' made the check red-on-day-one. Dormant groups are now reported and named, never judged - and the live-group arm is proven still armed by the same test.

edits.rationale: The dormancy rule, plus reporting it. Reported-and-NAMED rather than silently skipped, because a group the check has stopped judging must be visible or '0 findings' quietly becomes '0 findings among the groups I still look at' - the blind-check shape one level down from the one this file exists to close. Fails toward ALARMING on an unreadable timestamp: a clock we cannot read must not switch a check off.

The dormancy PAIR, which is the point: dormancy must silence the stale group WITHOUT silencing the live one. Testing only the first half would prove the check had been disarmed rather than corrected. Both directions mutation-proven, plus the unreadable-clock arm.

edits.rationale: The hand-run wrapper the reader's own error messages already name ('use scripts/audit-render-truncation.sh'). It builds the {runs, error_log_rows} object the stdin mode demands - the rows alone cannot prove the read was not blind. Its query is the SAME TEXT as renderTruncationRunsQuery deliberately: a wrapper fetching a different shape is a second definition of the check and it drifts. This is the script that found the dormancy defect before it shipped.
edits.sketch:
RUNS_JSON=$(PSQL "SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(t),'[]'::jsonb) FROM (
  SELECT COALESCE(domain,'(no domain)') AS domain,
         COALESCE(agent_type,'(no agent_type)') AS agent_type,
         COALESCE(NULLIF(context->>'coverage_mode',''),'(absent)') AS coverage_mode,
         COALESCE(context->>'window_first','') AS window_first,
         COALESCE((context->>'priority_not_live')::int,0) AS priority_not_live,
         occurred_at::text AS occurred_at
    FROM agent_error_log WHERE error_code='RENDER_AUDIT_TRUNCATED'
   ORDER BY domain, agent_type, occurred_at DESC) t;")
TOTAL=$(PSQL "SELECT count(*) FROM agent_error_log;")
printf '{"runs": %s, "error_log_rows": %s}' "$RUNS_JSON" "$TOTAL" | go run ./cmd/config-key-audit --render-truncation "$@"

plan.risks: THE DORMANCY RULE IS A DELIBERATE BLIND SPOT AND MUST BE READ AS ONE. A group silent for more than 14 days stops being judged, so a regression on a site that ALSO stops truncating would go unseen. That is the intended trade and it is bounded in a specific way: a site only stops writing these rows when it stops truncating, i.e. when it fits inside its cap, and a site inside its cap has no coverage debt to detect — the check's whole subject is absent. The residual case is a site that shrinks below the cap WHILE mis-configured; it would be silent here, and the config flip is visible in agent_definitions instead. Dormant groups are counted and NAMED in every run's doc_notes row precisely so this blind spot is legible rather than implicit. SECOND: 14 days is a judgement, not a measurement. It is ~4 missed opportunities at the 3-day per-site rotation cadence, chosen so a genuine regression still produces recent rows; if the rotation cadence changes this number should be revisited, and it is a single named constant so that is a one-line edit. THIRD: the arms judge only the MOST RECENT row per group, so a regression that has since self-corrected leaves no finding — deliberate, because the check answers 'is the estate right now correct', not 'has it ever been wrong'; the durable rows remain for anyone asking the historical question. FOURTH, the ordinary deployment risks: the image must be built and pushed before the overlay is applied or the CronJob sits in ImagePullBackOff, which this fleet reports as RUNNING rather than FAILED — that is why the service is in AGENT_DEPLOY_SERVICES, so the release path builds, pushes, retags and applies it in one ordered pass rather than by hand. FIFTH: this check reads agent_error_log and writes one doc_notes row per run; it takes no locks, mutates no work items and touches no site content, so its failure mode is silence rather than damage — which is exactly why the vacuity guard (an EMPTY agent_error_log refuses with exit 2 rather than reporting clean) is the load-bearing part of the design.
